definition: to take something for a short time and then give it back

hero.text: Pixel borrowed Bolt's map and gave it back after the trip.

everyday: Can I borrow your red crayon? I'll give it right back.

contrast.nonExample: Sara gave her old bike to her cousin to keep forever.
contrast.explanation: Her cousin keeps the bike forever, so it is a gift. To borrow is to take something and give it back later.

items.prompt: Which person borrows something?

options.text: Max buys a new ball at the store.
Lia uses her friend's pencil and gives it back.
Ken throws his old shoes away.

items.hint: When you borrow, you give the thing back.
items.explanation: Lia uses the pencil and gives it back. That is borrowing. Buying something means it is yours to keep.

wrong.a: Max buys the ball, so it is his to keep.
wrong.c: Throwing shoes away is not borrowing.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: I forgot my umbrella, so I ___ one from my teacher until the rain stopped.
items.hint: You use the umbrella only until the rain stops.
items.explanation: "Until the rain stopped" shows you used it for a short time and gave it back. That is borrowed.

items.prompt: Is this an example of borrowing?
items.passage: Jon took a book home from the library and returned it two weeks later.
items.hint: Did Jon give the book back?
items.explanation: Yes. Jon used the library book for a while and returned it. That is borrowing.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what borrow means.

chunks.text: I will bring it back after lunch.

items.hint: When you borrow, you give it back.
items.explanation: Borrowing means giving the thing back, so "I will bring it back after lunch" fits. Keeping it forever is not borrowing.

items.prompt: Which word best fits the sentence?
items.passage: Mom let me ___ her scarf for the day, and I gave it back that night.
items.hint: Which word means use it and then give it back?
items.explanation: "Gave it back that night" is the clue. Borrow means take something for a short time and return it. Keep means it stays yours.

hero.text: The night air was chilly, so Kai zipped up his hero jacket.

everyday: It was chilly in the morning, so I wore a sweater to school.

contrast.nonExample: The sand at the beach was hot under the bright sun.
contrast.explanation: Hot sand is warm, not cold. Chilly means a little bit cold.

items.prompt: Which day is chilly?

options.text: a cool fall morning when you need a jacket
a hot summer day at the pool
a warm day in a sunny garden

items.hint: Chilly means a little bit cold.
items.explanation: A cool morning when you need a jacket is a little cold. That is chilly. Hot and warm days are not chilly.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The room felt ___, so Dad closed the window.
items.hint: Why would Dad close a window?
items.explanation: Closing the window keeps cold air out. The room felt a little cold, so chilly fits.

items.prompt: Which word is the OPPOSITE of "chilly" in this sentence?
items.passage: The water in the lake was chilly.
items.hint: Find the word that means not cold.
items.explanation: Warm is the opposite of chilly. Cool means almost the same as chilly.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what chilly means.

chunks.text: so I put on my hat

items.hint: When it is chilly, you want to stay warm.
items.explanation: Chilly wind makes you want warm clothes like a hat and gloves. Taking off your shoes would make you colder.

items.prompt: Does this describe something chilly?
items.passage: Leo put his hand in the oven mitt and pulled out the hot bread.
items.hint: Is it a little cold, or hot?
items.explanation: No. Hot bread from the oven is the opposite of chilly. Chilly means a little bit cold.

definition: happy and bright in a way others can see

hero.text: Juniper gave a cheerful wave to every kid on the street.

everyday: Our bus driver is always cheerful and says good morning to everyone.

contrast.nonExample: Jay frowned and stomped to his room.
contrast.explanation: Frowning and stomping show a bad mood. A cheerful person is happy and bright.

items.prompt: Is this person cheerful?
items.passage: Ana smiles, hums a song, and says hello to everyone.
items.hint: Is Ana happy and bright?
items.explanation: Yes. Smiling, humming, and saying hello show Ana is happy. She is cheerful.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The yellow flowers made the room look bright and ___.
items.hint: "Bright and ___" — which word goes with bright and happy?
items.explanation: "Bright" is the clue. Yellow flowers make a room look happy and bright, so cheerful fits.

items.prompt: Which word is the OPPOSITE of "cheerful" in this sentence?
items.passage: Grandma was cheerful at her birthday party.
items.hint: Find the word for a bad mood.
items.explanation: Grumpy means in a bad mood, the opposite of cheerful. Happy means almost the same as cheerful.

items.prompt: "Cheerful" is made of "cheer" + "-ful." The ending "-ful" means "full of." So cheerful means:
items.hint: Put the parts together: full of + cheer.
items.explanation: -ful means full of, so cheerful means full of cheer. A cheerful person is happy and bright.

items.prompt: Which word best describes Zane?
items.passage: Zane whistled while he walked his dog. He grinned at everyone he passed.
items.hint: Whistling and grinning show a mood. Which one?
items.explanation: "Whistled" and "grinned at everyone" show Zane is happy and bright. He is cheerful.

definition: to look around a new place to learn about it

hero.text: Pixel and Kai explored the old tunnel to see where it led.

everyday: On our camping trip, we explored the woods and found a stream.

contrast.nonExample: Sam stayed on the couch and watched the same show again.
contrast.explanation: Sam is not going anywhere new or learning about a place. To explore is to look around a new place to learn about it.

items.prompt: Which person is exploring?

options.text: Jake looks all around a cave he has never seen before.
Eva eats a sandwich at home.

items.hint: To explore is to look around a new place.
items.explanation: Jake looks all around a new cave to learn about it. That is exploring.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: On the first day of school, we got to ___ our new classroom.
items.hint: The classroom is new. What do you do in a new place?
items.explanation: "New classroom" is the clue. You look around a new place to learn about it. That is explore.

items.prompt: Is this an example of exploring?
items.passage: The kids walked along the beach, looking at shells and tide pools they had never seen.
items.hint: Are they looking around to learn about a new place?
items.explanation: Yes. They look around a beach they have never seen and learn about it. That is exploring.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what explore means.

chunks.text: every corner of its new home

items.hint: To explore, you look around.
items.explanation: The puppy looks all around its new home, so it explores. Never leaving its box is not exploring.

items.prompt: Which word best fits what the scientists did?
items.passage: The scientists went deep under the sea in a small sub. They looked for fish no one had ever seen.
items.clue: looked for fish no one had ever seen
items.hint: They went to a new place to learn about it.
items.explanation: Going "deep under the sea" to look for new fish means they looked around a new place to learn. That is explored.

definition: to fix something that is broken

hero.text: Rex used his super strength to repair the broken bridge.

everyday: Dad repaired my bike's flat tire.

contrast.nonExample: Mo dropped the cup, and it cracked in two.
contrast.explanation: Dropping the cup broke it. To repair is to fix something that is broken.

items.prompt: What does "repair" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: Can you repair the broken toy car?
items.hint: The toy car is broken. What does it need?
items.explanation: To repair is to fix something that is broken. The broken car needs to be fixed.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The fence had a big hole, so Mom used boards to ___ it.
items.hint: What do you do to a fence with a hole?
items.explanation: "Big hole" means the fence is broken. Mom uses boards to fix it, so repair fits.

items.prompt: Which word means almost the same as "repaired" in this sentence?
items.passage: Grandpa repaired the leaky sink.
items.hint: Find the word that means made it work again.
items.explanation: Fixed means almost the same as repaired. Broke is the opposite.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what repair means.
items.hint: Repairing makes something whole again.
items.explanation: Tape fixes a torn page, so Kate repaired it. Ripping it more makes it worse, not repaired.

items.prompt: Is this an example of repairing?
items.passage: Lee cut his paper into tiny pieces for a craft.
items.hint: Is Lee fixing something broken?
items.explanation: No. Cutting paper for a craft is not fixing anything. To repair is to fix something that is broken.

hero.text: Bolt shared delicious pizza with the team after the rescue.

everyday: Grandma's warm apple pie smells delicious.

contrast.nonExample: The milk was old and tasted sour.
contrast.explanation: Sour, old milk tastes bad. Delicious means tasting or smelling very good.

items.prompt: Which food is delicious?
items.hint: Delicious means tasting very good.
items.explanation: A sweet, juicy strawberry tastes very good, so it is delicious. Burnt toast and soggy noodles do not taste good.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The soup was so ___ that I asked for another bowl.
items.hint: Why would you want another bowl?
items.explanation: "Asked for another bowl" shows the soup tasted very good. Delicious fits.

items.prompt: Which word means almost the same as "delicious" in this sentence?
items.passage: We ate delicious tacos at the fair.
items.hint: Which word is about tasting good?
items.explanation: Tasty means tasting good, like delicious. Spicy is a kind of taste, but spicy food is not always good to everyone.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what delicious means.
items.hint: Delicious food is food you want to eat.
items.explanation: Delicious cookies taste good, so you eat them all. Spitting them out means they tasted bad.

items.prompt: Which word best describes the bread?
items.passage: When the bread came out of the oven, it smelled so good that everyone ran into the kitchen.
items.hint: Everyone ran in because of the smell.
items.explanation: "Smelled so good" is the clue. Delicious means tasting or smelling very good.

hero.text: Nova checked the empty building to make sure no one was left inside.

everyday: My cereal bowl was empty after breakfast.

contrast.nonExample: The toy box was full of blocks and dolls.
contrast.explanation: A full box has many things inside. Empty means having nothing inside.

items.prompt: Which thing is empty?

options.text: a fish tank full of fish
a cookie jar with no cookies left

items.hint: Empty means nothing is inside.
items.explanation: A cookie jar with no cookies has nothing inside. It is empty. The fish tank and backpack are full.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Everyone went home, so the playground was ___.
items.hint: If everyone went home, who is left?
items.explanation: "Everyone went home" means no one is left. The playground is empty. Crowded means the opposite.

items.prompt: Which word is the OPPOSITE of "empty" in this sentence?
items.passage: I filled my empty water bottle at the sink.
items.hint: Find the word that means it has lots inside.
items.explanation: Full is the opposite of empty. Bare means almost the same as empty.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what empty means.

chunks.text: so the car could not go
so the car zoomed far away.

items.hint: An empty tank has no gas inside.
items.explanation: With no gas inside, the car cannot go. A car would not zoom away on an empty tank.

items.prompt: Is this thing empty?
items.passage: The bird's nest had three blue eggs in it.
items.hint: Is there anything inside the nest?
items.explanation: No. The nest has three eggs inside, so it is not empty. Empty means having nothing inside.

hero.text: Kai hid the map inside a hollow log in the forest.

everyday: An owl made its home in a hollow tree.

contrast.nonExample: The brick was solid all the way through.
contrast.explanation: A solid brick has no space inside. Hollow means having an empty space inside, like a tube or a drum.

items.prompt: Which thing is hollow?

options.text: a tube from a paper towel roll

items.hint: Hollow means there is empty space inside.
items.explanation: A paper towel tube has empty space in the middle, so it is hollow. A rock and a brick are solid all the way through.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The chocolate bunny was ___, so it had nothing but air inside.
items.hint: "Nothing but air inside" is a big clue.
items.explanation: "Nothing but air inside" means the bunny has an empty space inside. That is hollow.

items.prompt: Which word fits best?
items.passage: The log looked whole, but it had a big empty space in the middle. The log was ___.
items.hint: Which word means having an empty space inside?
items.explanation: "Empty space in the middle" tells you the log is hollow. Solid means filled all the way through, the opposite.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what hollow means.

chunks.text: so it makes a loud boom
so it is filled with sand.

items.hint: A hollow drum has empty space inside.
items.explanation: The empty space inside a hollow drum helps it boom. If it were filled with sand, it would not be hollow.

items.prompt: Is this thing hollow?
items.passage: Ivy found a big seashell with an empty space inside where a crab could hide.
items.hint: Is there an empty space inside?
items.explanation: Yes. The shell has an empty space inside, so it is hollow.

definition: to smell something by taking short breaths through your nose

hero.text: Juniper's dog sniffed the trail to find the missing hiker.

everyday: I sniffed the flowers to see if they smelled sweet.

contrast.nonExample: Ben listened to the birds singing outside.
contrast.explanation: Ben is using his ears, not his nose. To sniff is to smell by taking short breaths through your nose.

items.prompt: What does "sniff" mean in this sentence?
items.passage: The rabbit stopped to sniff the carrot.
items.hint: Which body part do you use to sniff?
items.explanation: To sniff is to smell with short breaths through your nose. The rabbit smells the carrot.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: Mom opened the milk to ___ it and see if it was still fresh.
items.clue: see if it was still fresh
items.hint: How can you tell if milk is fresh without tasting it?
items.explanation: You can smell milk to tell if it is fresh. "See if it was still fresh" is the clue. Sniff fits.

items.prompt: Is this an example of sniffing?
items.passage: The puppy put its nose to the ground and smelled every patch of grass.
items.hint: Is the puppy smelling with its nose?
items.explanation: Yes. The puppy uses its nose to smell the grass. That is sniffing.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what sniff means.
items.hint: Sniffing is about smelling.
items.explanation: When you sniff, you smell things, like cookies baking. Hearing a drum is about your ears, not your nose.

items.prompt: Which word best fits what the bear did?
items.passage: The bear lifted its nose and breathed in quickly, again and again. It was trying to smell the honey.
items.clue: breathed in quickly; trying to smell
items.hint: The bear used its nose with quick breaths.
items.explanation: "Breathed in quickly" with its nose "to smell the honey" is sniffing.

definition: strong and hard to break or knock over

hero.text: Rex built a sturdy wall that the strong wind could not knock down.

everyday: We need a sturdy box to carry these heavy books.

contrast.nonExample: The paper cup crushed when Ty squeezed it.
contrast.explanation: A paper cup breaks easily. Sturdy means strong and hard to break.

items.prompt: Which thing is sturdy?

options.text: a tower made of wet tissue paper

items.hint: Sturdy means strong and hard to break.
items.explanation: A strong wooden table is hard to break or knock over. It is sturdy. Bubbles and wet tissue break very easily.

items.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence.
items.passage: The tree house was so ___ that five kids could play in it safely.
items.hint: Five kids can play in it safely. What kind of tree house is that?
items.explanation: "Five kids could play in it safely" shows it was strong. Sturdy fits. A tiny tree house could not hold five kids.

items.prompt: Which word is the OPPOSITE of "sturdy" in this sentence?
items.passage: Grandpa sat on the sturdy chair.
items.hint: Find the word that means easy to break.
items.explanation: Weak is the opposite of sturdy. Strong means almost the same as sturdy.

items.prompt: Build a sentence that shows what sturdy means.
items.hint: Sturdy things are strong.
items.explanation: Sturdy boots are strong, so they keep feet safe on rocks. Boots that rip right away are not sturdy.

items.prompt: Is this thing sturdy?
items.passage: The sand castle fell apart as soon as a small wave touched it.
items.hint: Was it strong and hard to knock over?
items.explanation: No. The sand castle fell apart easily. Sturdy means strong and hard to break or knock over.
